subject_session: pooled 15 sessions / 5 mice (prototype + GLM: sub-LA11 ses-1)
stated_limitation: The main limitation is the stimulus set. Five frequencies spaced one octave apart at a single 60 dB level are enough to establish frequency selectivity and to locate a best frequency to within an octave, but not to resolve tuning bandwidth or the level dependence of a full frequency-response area. The archived files also do not carry electrode depth or channel position for the sorted units, so the tonotopic gradient along the probe cannot be reconstructed from them.

justification.dataset: 000986 is the canonical known-good mouse auditory-cortex pure-tone dataset for frequency tuning.
justification.handling: Data streamed correctly with exact interval counting and gap exclusion, but no explicit unit quality filtering is applied beyond statistical response classification.
justification.analysis: Appropriate nonparametric tests plus a split-half best-frequency control that directly addresses selection bias, and held-out GLM encoding/decoding.
justification.correctness: All headline counts and statistics reproduce from the committed CSV/logs/figures, with only a minor denominator ambiguity between the 1160 tuned and 1081 responsive-and-tuned units.
justification.figures: Figures 1-5 show the effect clearly with units, sample sizes, and category-chosen representative examples; only the disclosed fig06 is stale.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate and the write-up names specific limitations, candidly flagging the fig06 configuration mismatch, the unexecuted notebook, and the stimulus-set constraints.
justification.verdict: The phenomenon is demonstrated overwhelmingly and honestly, well above rotation-student quality, so I would take the descriptive result and move on.
